name: Trisikkha Insight Meditation Center

location.address: 4207 US Hwy 92 W, Plant City, FL 33563

technique: Formal sitting and walking meditation with morning and evening Pali-Thai chanting, taught step by step over a structured multi-day course under the Eight Precepts and Noble Silence
teacherAccess: Daily Dhamma talks by Ajarn Willie with a dedicated question period after each talk; participants are taught in small groups and have the opportunity to work one-on-one with the instructor during the retreat.
retreatOptions: Residential meditation retreats held roughly quarterly, most around 10-12 days long (e.g., a 12-day English-language course); partial attendance is discouraged but participants are advised to at least arrive at the start if they cannot stay the full course. Sunday sessions are offered between retreats.
schedule: 03:00 wake-up; 04:00-07:00 morning chanting and sitting/walking meditation; breakfast and volunteer tasks; 09:00-11:30 Dhamma talk; lunch and volunteer tasks; 13:30-16:00 sitting/walking meditation; break; 18:00-21:00 evening chanting and meditation.
cost: Free — retreats are run entirely on a donation (dana) basis; no course fees are charged.

pricePerDay.notes: Strictly donation-based. The center states there is no charge for its retreats; donations are offered voluntarily near the end of the course, so no set per-night rate is determinable.

workNotes: Participants are asked to volunteer for cleaning and support tasks during daily break periods; not strictly mandatory but presented as an integral part of practice.
foodNotes: Breakfast and lunch are provided free of charge (no food after midday, per the Eight Precepts); the menu emphasizes meatless dishes, though broths and seasonings may occasionally contain animal derivatives, and participants with allergies or dietary restrictions may bring their own food.
about: Trisikkha Insight Meditation Center is a Theravada Buddhist retreat center on about 17 acres of wooded, canal-side land in Plant City, east of Tampa, run as the U.S. sister site of Trisikkha Petchaburi in Thailand. Retreats are led by Ajarn Willie and follow a traditional Thai Vipassana course structure: participants commit to the full length of the course (typically 10-12 days), observe the Eight Precepts and Noble Silence, and follow a fixed daily schedule of chanting, sitting, and walking meditation interspersed with Dhamma talks and question periods. Men and women are housed separately in sleeping halls or in a dedicated camping area, with meditation mats, sleeping mats, and tents provided. Teachings are mostly in Thai, with dedicated English-language courses offered periodically, and the retreat is entirely donation-supported, with breakfast and lunch provided free of charge. The center also hosts drop-in Sunday sessions between its scheduled retreats.
